articles.title: Tony Pulis column: Why managers can learn a lot from leaders like Napoleon Bonaparte
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains what he did between jobs and why out-of-work managers can learn a lot from leaders outside of football.
articles.body:
The November international break is almost upon us, which always means one thing - the managerial merry-go-round is about to properly get into gear.

It's known as 'sacking season' for a reason - the new campaign has started to take shape and I know from experience that any manager who is not winning games will always be sleeping with just one eye closed, and the other one open.

At any club on a poor run of results, the owners and supporters will be questioning whether the manager is the right fit to continue.

This two-week break from domestic games is the ideal opportunity to blood the new incumbent and give them a period of getting to know everyone before the games start up again.

That means it is 'hiring season' too, but there are always far more out-of-work managers than vacant positions.

Since the start of last season, 60 different managers have resigned or been sacked by teams in the Premier League and Football League. Three of them left to take up offers from other clubs but, in total, 37 of them - or 62% - are not currently in management.

For most managers, it's rarely the case where you walk into a new club within a few weeks of leaving your last one, so what do out-of-work managers do between jobs to make sure they are ready to take the next opportunity that fits?

It is more than 32 years since I received my marching orders from my first job at Bournemouth , who were in what is now known as League One. I was devastated.

I had - as I always did - given everything I could do to benefit the club, and with it being my first sacking I honestly did not know where my next step would take me.

But, on the second day of me being out of work, my home phone rang and at the end of the line was Jim Smith, who was in charge of Portsmouth, a few miles down the south coast.

I knew Jim then, but not really well. I'd been a manager for two years, but by then he had already spent 25 years in the dugout, at eight different clubs.

He asked how I was and, before I could even reply, recited these immortal words, which always stuck with me - "son, you're not a real manager until you get sacked at least three times - so get your backside off the sofa and get on with getting another job" - then he put the phone down!

I've used that sentence myself many times since to managers who have lost their job and are struggling to come to terms with it.

That can happen a lot. People outside the game maybe don't realise how difficult it can be when you are sacked, and how it affects certain individuals differently - you can easily fall off the merry-go-round and, as a manager, you never know for sure whether you will get another chance.

'When you are out of work, you can still learn a lot'

Someone else who phoned me up in the summer of 1994 was another great name in the game as a player and manager, Bruce Rioch.

At the time, Bruce was having a lot of success as manager of Bolton - he would get the Arsenal job a few months later - and he asked me if I would scout for him while I was trying to find my next manager's post.

He was very keen to get me involved and very helpful in keeping me busy watching games.

I was equally keen on helping Bruce and ended up scouting for him for that entire season. To this day, I owe him so much in respect of what he asked me to do, because of what I learned during that time.

Football is the best team sport in the world and the fundamental thing I picked up that season is that its 'product', the players, were the secret to success.

By that, I mean that I realised that at all levels there are good players, and at all levels there are managers working on budgets. I learned that knowing the level you were at, and placing the right players at that level who you could afford, would be an enormous factor in your chances of success, or failure.

Yes, there is more to it than that - you then also had to pick good characters, coach them well and motivate them with a driving force they could handle and enjoy - but you have to start by getting the right players for the level you are at.

The following summer, I was appointed manager of Gillingham, who had just finished 89th out of the 92 clubs across the top four divisions.

I was lucky enough to inherit a club who had quite a few players out of contract, so it enabled me to reset the first team with several players I had watched during my time scouting for Bruce and Bolton.

All the hours and miles I travelled that year paid off, with Gillingham finishing second in what is now League Two and gaining promotion in my first season. Those players who we recruited kick-started four years of my managerial career in Kent, and left me with some fantastic on-field memories.

My time and success at Priestfield opened up an ever-revolving door of work and rest.

Whenever I was out of work in the years that followed, watching games still occupied my midweeks and weekends for the same reasons as before - I wanted to watch players who I might end up signing.

Lots of games I went to were watched from the terraces with either home or away supporters, which was always interesting and illuminating - I've always valued the views of match-going fans on different players.

Down the years, I was also invited to spend a few weeks coaching abroad, in Kuwait and the United States, by friends I had in the game.

Whatever I was doing, I always felt like I was learning, and not just by watching football around the world. I became an avid reader of sports books and also finding out about great leaders of men through history.

So, as well as visiting Bayer Leverkusen, Athletic Bilbao and RB Leipzig - who back then had only just started their rise from the bottom tier of German football - I would analyse and investigate historic battles or events.

Napoleon Bonaparte really kept me busy. His attention to detail and his command of his generals was only superseded by his troop's loyalty to him - they would literally die for him!

His 250th birthday was celebrated in Corsica in the summer of 2019, and a French newspaper invited me to go along and give a British perspective on how we see Napoleon as a leader and a person.

I was delighted to accept and was amazed by how many people from all over Europe turned up too.

Hated by many countries, but still adored by his followers, Napoleon also produced the Napoleonic Code, which is still the foundation of French civil law today.

'It's better to be in a job than out of football full-stop'

As well as great military triumphs, I studied defeats too - they are as much a part of football management as victories, after all - and you can compare the organisational brilliance of Napoleon to the disaster of the Battle of Balaclava and the Charge of the Light Brigade.

One summer, I travelled out to Crimea to witness the scene of that tragic charge by the bravest of brave men.

Lord Raglan, the British commander-in-chief, was based on the high ground and could see everything in the Russian positions and the brigades.

His order to attack was ambiguous and although Lord Cardigan, who led the charge, questioned it, he still followed it through - leading to one of the most infamous military disasters in history.

It should never have happened but, just as in football, leadership and communication from the top was key. The instructions were passed down from Raglan to Lord Lucan to Cardigan and became garbled - too many cooks, in my opinion!

The last book which really stuck with me, in terms of inspiring me as a leader, was the story of HMS Endurance - disaster strikes during a journey through the ice fields of the southern hemisphere when the ship becomes stuck.

I cannot do justice to the deeds of Sir Ernest Shackleton in this column but his leadership of his men, along with his number two Frank Worsley, was extraordinary.

Both dovetailed in a way that gave their men the energy, desire and determination to believe and follow instructions in the most appalling conditions, never once questioning their leaders' abilities to help them survive.

Over the years, I've never stopped reading about, or watching, great leaders like that - there is so much that young coaches can learn from other sports or history that will benefit then, the same way it did me.

Going to games was still the most important thing when I was between jobs, because I would always believe my own eyes when watching players.

There were times when that became more of a challenge, especially at the back end of my career, but times change and if you are not in tune with what is happening in the game then you can get dropped very quickly.

But I am sure that most of my managerial compatriots would also agree with me that experience in all walks of life can be invaluable.

I learned so much when I was out of work, about all aspects of leadership, individually and collectively.

My advice to managers out of work now is the same that I received from Jim, all those years ago - pick yourselves up and get off the sofa to get back in work as quickly as possible.

You should never be afraid of dropping down a level the way I did, too. It is better to get a job, any job, than be out of football full-stop. That hasn't changed since my day, either.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

articles.summary: El riojano dará la convocatoria para el cierre de la fase grupos de la Nations League
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente anunciará este viernes 6 de noviembre, a partir de las 11:30 horas, la convocatoria de la Selección española para los dos últimos partidos de la fase de grupos de la UEFA Nations League, ante República Checa e Inglaterra. Posteriormente, a las 12:30 horas, el seleccionador comparecerá ante los medios de comunicación en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano para explicar los nombres elegidos. La convocatoria podrá seguirse a través de los canales oficiales de la Selección española y de la RFEF, que publicarán los nombres de los futbolistas seleccionados a las 11:30 horas. La posterior rueda de prensa de Luis de la Fuente, prevista para las 12:30 horas, también podrá seguirse a través de los canales oficiales de la Federación. La Selección española afrontará sus dos últimos compromisos de la fase de grupos de la Nations League: España ya tiene asegurada su clasificación para los cuartos de final, pero todavía debe resolver si termina como primera o segunda de grupo.

articles.title: FA Cup: How to watch and listen to first round on the BBC this weekend
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything experts explain how to follow the FA Cup first round on TV and radio this weekend.
articles.body:
After six rounds of preliminary and qualifying matches, the first round proper of the FA Cup gets under way from Friday.

A total of 40 matches will be played during the long weekend, beginning with two games on Friday, followed by 33 on Saturday, four on Sunday, and one on Monday.

Premier League and Championship teams do not enter the competition until the third round, which is designated to start on 9 January 2027.

Here is how you can watch, listen and keep across all the action on the BBC.

The BBC will be showing two of the first-round fixtures live - with both available on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer.

In the first of those, National League side Altrincham carry a reputation for giant-killing into their match with League One's Notts County on Saturday.

The non-league side have claimed 17 wins against league opposition, more than any other club that have never been part of the top four divisions.

Notts County are the world's oldest professional league team and won the FA Cup in 1894.

In the second BBC televised game of the weekend, Cray Wanderers of the Isthmian League meet League One high-flyers Stockport County on Sunday.

Reputed to be London's oldest football club - pre-dating the FA Cup itself - it is the first time seventh-tier Cray have made it to the first round.

Altrincham v Notts County - coverage from 17:15, kick-off 17:30

Cray Wanderers v Stockport County - coverage from 14:00, kick-off 14:15

A live highlights show hosted by Jason Mohammad will round up the weekend's action on Sunday from 17:10 on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer, including 2021 FA Cup winners Leicester's visit to sixth-tier Oxford City.

Live text commentary will cover all of the weekend's action, while digital highlights will be available on the BBC Sport website, app and social media channels.

There will be eight ties shown live on television across the weekend, with the remaining six games being broadcast on TNT Sports.

BBC local radio stations will have commentaries of selected matches from the first round, available on BBC Sounds.

Five games have also been selected for coverage on BBC 5 Sports Extra, Sports Extra 2 and Sports Extra 3.

articles.title: Óskarsson: "Estoy contento con el gol, pero quiero marcar más, fallo mucho"
articles.standfirst: El delantero islandés, que suma cinco tantos este curso, los últimos cuatro en el último mes, se exige aprovechar más y mejor las ocasiones que suele tener
articles.summary: El delantero islandés, que suma cinco tantos este curso, los últimos cuatro en el último mes, se exige aprovechar más y mejor las ocasiones que suele tener
articles.body: Orri Óskarsson está contento por estar marcando goles con asiduidad, pero aún así hace autocrítica y considera que debe meter más, porque está fallando demasiadas ocasiones. El delantero islandés quiso hacer una lectura positiva del punto sumado por la Real Sociedad contra el Olympique de Lyon. Óskarsson quiso dar valor también al punto sumado ante el Olympique de Lyon. “Ellos son un buen equipo, con mucha calidad también. Jugamos un buen partido, especialmente en la primera mitad. Creo que pudimos sacar los tres puntos pero un punto contra este equipo, de mucha calidad, está bien. Estábamos un poquito cansados y el árbitro pitó demasiadas faltas, por eso bajamos en la segunda mitad”. El 9 de la Real destacó su conexión con Barrenetxea, que le hizo un espectacular centro en la jugada en la que marcó. “Entrenamos juntos todos los días, es un gran futbolista y tenemos una buena relación dentro y fuera del campo. Estoy contento con mi juego, pero mi trabajo es ayudar al equipo en estas situaciones para ayudar a ganar y sumar los puntos”. Le comentaron a Óskarsson que en este 2026 ha hecho 15 dianas produciendo 14 ‘expected goals’. “Quiero meter más, está claro, fallo muchas ocasiones y no estoy contento con esto, pero es parte del trabajo de los puntas, he visto muchas veces a Mbappé, Rafinha y los mejores, y fallo mucho. Pero lo que es importante para mí es tener las situaciones para meter y ahora tengo la sensación de poder tenerlas durante todo el partido”. El delantero txuriurdin quiere apurar las opciones de entrar en el top 8 hasta el final de la fase Liga. “Claro que es el objetivo, queremos terminar en el top 8 para ir directamente a los octavos de final. Ahora no tenemos los puntos para ello, pero quedan cuatro partidos más”.

articles.title: Revuelta popular en el Leicester City contra la polémica embajadora de su principal patrocinador
articles.standfirst: "El Leicester City Football Club reconoce las preocupaciones planteadas en torno a los acontecimientos recientes"
articles.summary: "El Leicester City Football Club reconoce las preocupaciones planteadas en torno a los acontecimientos recientes"
articles.body: El Leicester City que compite en la EFL League One ha emitido un comunicado en el que admite sentir "preocupación" después de que su patrocinador principal (BC.GAME) nombrara a Eva Elfie, famosa actriz de cine para adultos, como embajadora. 'The Foxes Trust', un conocido grupo de animación del Leicester City, expresó su "consternación" ante la noticia confirmada por BC.GAME de nombrar a Eva Elfie, "creadora de contenido internacional y personalidad de los deportes electrónicos", como su embajadora. "A estas alturas, la mayoría de los seguidores del Leicester City ya conocerán la consternación y el descontento de la asociación de aficionados ante el hecho de que BC.GAME sea nuestro patrocinador principal en la parte frontal de la camiseta. Desde el momento en que el club decidió aceptar el patrocinio de una empresa de apuestas, sentimos que el Leicester City estaba abandonando sus valores. Si a esto le sumamos que BC Game ha establecido una colaboración con alguien que se ha dado a conocer a través de contenido para adultos, la situación se complica aún más. Tanto los juegos de azar como la pornografía pueden tener efectos devastadores en la vida de las personas, especialmente en la de los jóvenes", compartieron los 'The Foxes Trust'. Los 'Foxes' firmaron un acuerdo de patrocinio BC Game, plataforma de casino 'on line', en el verano de 2024. La empresa que tiene a Eva Elfie como embajadora ha sido el patrocinador de la camiseta del Leicester City durante las últimas tres temporadas. El Leicester ha abordado la situación y ha señalado que busca encontrar una "resolución mutuamente aceptable". "El Leicester City Football Club reconoce las preocupaciones planteadas en torno a los acontecimientos recientes relacionados con nuestro socio principal, BC.GAME. Hemos trasladado estas preocupaciones directamente a BC.GAME y seguimos manteniendo conversaciones con la empresa para buscar una solución mutuamente aceptable", compartió el club inglés.

articles.title: Coventry: Sky Blues' Premier League survival chances growing after recent form
articles.summary: Coventry City could move 11th in the Premier League with victory at Everton on Friday as Frank Lampard returns to the Toffees with his side growing in confidence.
articles.body:
"I would like to think there is a higher ceiling," says Frank Lampard.

After four opening defeats without scoring, a run which had Coventry written off, the Sky Blues are finding their feet.

They could move up to 11th in the Premier League with victory at Everton on Friday as Lampard returns to the Toffees, who he managed for a year from January 2022.

A win would leave them on 12 points, level with eighth-placed Bournemouth , a quarter of the way through their first season back in the Premier League in 25 years.

Just Middlesbrough (1996-97), Burnley (2009-10) and Cardiff (2013-14) have been relegated from the Premier League after taking 12 points from 10 games.

History is on Coventry 's side as last season's Championship winners look to prove the doubters wrong.

Despite Coventry 's start to the season - after defeats by Arsenal , Hull , Manchester City and Brighton - the optimism at the training ground did not waver.

The positive mood at the club's Ryton base remains, following Saturday's victory over Sunderland , as it did after the 5-0 home thumping by Brighton .

It was accepted the game, where Coventry played almost 45 minutes with 10 men following Taiwo Awoniyi's dismissal, can happen in the Premier League - and there was no hangover.

There was a belief there was enough evidence in performances against Hull , Manchester City and Arsenal the Sky Blues could compete in the top flight.

Then, after a 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat by Aston Villa , Lampard tweaked the system to match Nottingham Forest 's back three to earn a 1-0 win at the City Ground.

"The result sometimes you can't quite control, but you can control your idea going into a game, that maximises our strengths and looks at the opposition's," said Lampard, who is in before 7.30am every morning, using the gym before training.

"There can be various reasons why we do it. We went to Nottingham Forest and we matched up their formation because I wasn't keen to go there in the moment we were in with a back four and the problems they can give you with wing-backs and 10s.

"It's not just my, or our, choice on formation which is going to win or lose games. We know we have a big fight so every small percentage in our set-up if we feel that way we will do it - but we must feel it's going to be the right one."

Lampard has always been tactically flexible and three wins in five games has allowed Coventry to climb out of the relegation zone.

The stats provide interesting reading too, especially when compared with the 1-0 defeat by Hull which could have been so damaging in the first home game of the season.

Then, Coventry had 68.5% possession but that dropped to 42.6% in the 3-1 win over Sunderland . The Sky Blues also made more than 200 fewer passes and more than 50 fewer forward passes against the Black Cats.

Their passes in the final third more than halved from 128 to just 60, as the patience - and even pragmatism - paid off as the Sky Blues begin to understand the demands of the division.

The benching of skipper Matt Grimes, key in last season's promotion, was also a big call from Lampard but one which has been met with understanding from within.

Coventry still have the lowest xG (expected goals) in the Premier League of 8.34 but lessons have been learned from the frustration of the opening weeks, even if those at the club recognise the difficult start given three of their opening four away games were at Manchester City , Arsenal and Tottenham .

After Everton , Coventry host Crystal Palace and Ipswich either side of a trip to Leeds to complete a run sources felt would be crucial to their survival hopes.

"When you're in the zone, enjoyment of the win is pretty short-lived - you switch your attention to the next game. Relaxation and complacency is the biggest danger in this game," said Lampard.

"If we can keep the strength of feeling, even when difficult results come, we will give ourselves a chance."

Inexperienced Sky Blues looking for resilience

One Premier League manager has privately said if he were to take any players from Coventry , one of them would be Jack Rudoni.

The former Huddersfield midfielder - playing in League One four years ago - has been one of the quickest players to adapt for Coventry , with four goals in 10 appearances in all competitions, in a group short of top-flight experience.

Awoniyi (90 games) and Ethan Pinnock (117) have played the most with just Loum Tchaouna, Ellis Simms, Matt Grimes, Kaine Kesler-Hayden, Dan Bentley and Gus Hamer having featured in the Premier League.

Even then, Simms only made 12 appearances for Everton , Grimes just four for Swansea, Bentley 10 for Wolves and Kesler-Hayden had only played five minutes.

Tchaouna's and Hamer's experiences were relegation with Burnley and Sheffield United.

Lampard knew they would need time to find the grit to stay in the top flight but the Sky Blues have given themselves the chance.

"Sometimes you go through hundreds of games to find that resilience and a lot of our players haven't had that," added Lampard.

"There have been some complications. The squad and ourselves have managed pretty well when you see what we're trying to do."

articles.title: La Real debe pasar a 12 equipos para llegar al top 8
articles.standfirst: El octavo puesto está a sólo dos puntos, pero hay una docena de clubes por el medio y del séptimo lugar para arriba ya se han puesto muy difíciles de alcanzar
articles.summary: El octavo puesto está a sólo dos puntos, pero hay una docena de clubes por el medio y del séptimo lugar para arriba ya se han puesto muy difíciles de alcanzar
articles.body: El empate que la Real Sociedad tuvo en Anoeta contra el Olympique de Lyon le ha hecho descender al conjunto txuriurdin de la decimocuarta posición a la vigésima y, por tanto, tener una docena de equipos por encima hasta el top 8, así que deberá pasar a todos ellos en las cuatro jornadas que restan, para lograr ese objetivo. La parte positiva es que el octavo puesto está a sólo dos puntos, con 12 por jugarse. Las cuentas de la lechera dicen que, habiendo ganado al OL, la Real podría estar ahora mismo cerrando ese top 8 o, al menos, en el grupo de seis equipos con los siete puntos que te ponen en esa posición, entre los que están, por cierto, los franceses. El problema para los txuriurdin es que el séptimo clasificado, que es ni más ni menos que el Bayer Leverkusen está ya cuatro por encima, y cinco de margen tienen Juventus, Olympiacos y, aunque parezca increíble, una Union Saint-Gilloise con la que empató el equipo de Matarazzo en su campo belga y que no pareció para tanto. Benfica, Bournemouth y Ferencváros han hecho 12 de 12 y tienen muy encarrilada su presencia entre los mejores. Con esa situación clasificatoria, parece evidente que la próxima jornada, en Londres ante el Crystal Palace, que es vigesimoprimero, se antoja decisiva en las aspiraciones de la Real, que luego recibiría en Anoeta al Torreense, que está justo un puesto por encima, y al Viktoria Plzen, trigésimo en a día de hoy, seis puntos que está obligada a sumar, para ver si luego puede jugarse el estar en el top 8 en la jornada final en el campo de la Juventus.

articles.summary: Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds travel to Burton Albion looking to add a glorious chapter to their FA Cup fairytale.
articles.body:
The notion of your football club ceasing to exist is unthinkable for many fans, but for supporters of Rushden & Diamonds it became a sad reality in 2011.

The Northamptonshire-based side, backed by the late Max Griggs, rocketed through non-league in the 1990s and in 2003 reached the third tier of English football before financial issues after he stepped away ultimately saw them fold.

A community lost its focal point, and within years their Nene Park stadium had been razed to the ground.

"It was heartbreaking - we knew we'd been robbed." reflected Rob Usher, the chairman of phoenix side AFC Rushden & Diamonds, who will make their FA Cup first-round debut this weekend.

"I think it was that anger that probably fuelled the fans saying 'no, we don't accept it. We're not gone, we're not done and we want our club back."

Some 2,000 travelling fans will make their way to see the now eighth-tier Diamonds take on League One side Burton Albion on Saturday - a bittersweet reminder of days the supporters of the original club could have once taken for granted.

Usher, like many of those involved with the Northern Premier League Division One Midlands side, has followed both incarnations of the club - firstly as a fan, but also as a groundsman and turnstile operator before becoming chairman in 2022.

"My first game was an FA Cup tie against Shrewsbury Town in 1998. It was the year we ended up playing Leeds United in the third round." he said.

"Rushden & Diamonds gave us some great times. Winning leagues, the Duane Darby's, the Onandi Lowe's of our past. But I tell everyone I've never traded for what we have with AFC Rushden & Diamonds.

"This is a community, this is an army of people who turn up and give their time and their money, their care, their devotion... not because they want the club to exist, but because they want the club to thrive. That's why it's so special".

Diamonds, who now play their home games at Hayden Road, started their journey to the first round proper with a 5-0 win at Kimberley Miners Welfare in the extra preliminary round on 8 August.

They have also beaten Long Eaton United, Desborough Town, Peterborough Sports, Braintree Town and Morecambe to reach this stage.

Along with Stafford Rangers, who host Grimsby Town on Sunday, they are the only side left in the competition to have played from the earliest round and have so far earned £23,194 from the FA's prize fund.

The winners of the tie at Burton's Pirelli Stadium will collect £47,750, with the losers taking £15,800.

Joining AFC Rushden & Diamonds' attempt to make more history will be Billy Sharp, the Championship's all-time record goalscorer, who has reversed his recent decision to retire.

The 40-year-old, best known for his spells with Sheffield United and Doncaster Rovers, scored his first nine professional goals while on loan from the Blades to the original Diamonds in 2005.

"They [Rushden & Diamonds] made me as a player," said Sharp, who will be targeting a landmark 300th goal while filling in for forward James Clifton who is serving a suspension for accumulated yellow cards.

Diamonds' FA Cup story too hard to turn down - Sharp

Retired Sheff Utd legend Sharp signs for Rushden

"I've stayed in contact with the club over last few years, I should've been here for a legends game and I couldn't make it. But I always look out for their results.

"Elliot [Sandy, the club's manager] asked me if I'd consider playing, I said let's see what happens v Morecambe. Within 20 minutes of the result he text me an eyes emoji.

"I just smiled and said give me a day or two. It just seemed right. The opportunity to score another goal, to play another game in the FA Cup. It's special. This club means a lot to me, it gave me my chance when I was a young kid. Hopefully we can cause a shock, if we get through to the next round James [Clifton] can get his chance."

Defender Sam Brown, who grew up watching Rushden & Diamonds on the terraces at Nene Park, remembers chanting Sharp's name and expects it to feel "weird" to now play alongside him.

Brown was involved in the phoenix club's inaugural season and has made 350 appearances across two spells.

"It's been a rollercoaster," he said. "It's a big journey and I'm glad to have been a part of it.

"The club is owned by the fans so it needs all the fans to pull together to be able to grow. They turn up every Saturday no matter where we are and it's nice to have a chance for them to enjoy a different kind of environment on Saturday."

While the travelling supporters will hope to see an upset against Burton, for many, the experience of bringing their community together for such an occasion will provide the most lasting memories.

Diamonds say they have put on six coaches "at cost price" to help transport fans to the game in east Staffordshire.

Many are part owners and volunteers, including husband and wife Teresa and David Hales who help look after the club's kit.

"It's brilliant, absolutely brilliant." said Teresa. "For a little club like us it's absolutely amazing. I'm just so proud of everybody. Players, volunteers, everybody.

"There have been times over the years where I've sat with my head in my hands thinking, 'oh God, what's going to happen next?' But we're on the way up. We're really on the way up."

"It would be the shock of shocks," said club chairman Usher. "I've seen this squad this year pull off unbelievable things when the odds are against us, so I don't count us out.

"I've seen this club come back from death quite literally in 2011 and once again four years ago [when the phoenix club faced financial troubles].

"Diamonds are never done. Diamonds are forever."

What happened to the original Rushden & Diamonds?

Rushden & Diamonds were formed in 1992 following the merger of Rushden Town and Irthlingborough Diamonds.

The merger was the brainchild of Max Griggs, the owner of Northamptonshire-based Dr. Martens, with the aim of getting the single, larger club into the Football League.

The club reached the Conference, now known as the National League, in 1996 and realised Griggs' dream of EFL football in 2001 under the management of Brian Talbot.

In 2003, Diamonds were promoted as champions to Division Two, now known as League One, but Griggs' retirement as chairman signalled the beginning of their ultimate demise.

By 2006 they had been relegated back to non-league and mounting financial pressures saw them kicked out the Conference in 2011 before ultimately folding.

Rivals Kettering Town moved into the club's Nene Park stadium at Irthlingborough for a brief and ill-fated period between 2011 and 2012, before the ground was demolished in 2017.

articles.title: Manchester United reporter notebook: Shea Lacey and Old Trafford young guns offer Michael Carrick hope of unlikely revival
articles.summary: Shea Lacey's impressive cameo against Roma offered Michael Carrick fresh hope of an unlikely Manchester United revival; the 19-year-old's impact underlined why the academy graduate deserves a starting role against Aston Villa as Carrick considers putting his faith in youth
articles.body:
Whether the feeling proves short-lived or sparks something bigger for Michael Carrick and Manchester United remains to be seen, but it was important to see a stadium that has been starved of moments to celebrate this season roaring again.

There was plenty to dissect from the comeback win over Roma , but one of the biggest positives for Carrick was the impressive 15-minute cameo from 19-year-old Shea Lacey.

Lacey came on with the drive, confidence and quality to take responsibility and push United forward. His inch-perfect pass to Matheus Cunha was pivotal in setting up the winner.

It was a moment he had been working towards since the age of eight, when he first chose to join United's academy.

His family, who are originally from Liverpool, allowed him to make his own decision about where he wanted to play his football. He chose the red side of Manchester.

Having worked his way through the age groups at Carrington, despite a few injury setbacks along the way, it was already evident last season that Lacey was ready for the step up to senior football.

Having watched him extensively at U21 level, I have always been struck by the confidence he carries on the pitch. It is not just his trademark move of cutting inside from the right flank onto his left foot that stands out. His vision, spatial awareness and finishing are all qualities that could make him an excellent fit for a United side lacking creativity.

He has the work-rate to match, too. Since beginning to train with the first team permanently last season, Lacey has put plenty of work in behind the scenes to ease his transition into senior football.

He has shown real dedication in the gym and in the kitchen to prepare himself for the physical demands of the men's game. He has also regularly stayed behind after training to do extra work with senior players and coaching staff, including Travis Binnion, who knows the youngster well from his time coaching him at U21 level.

That dedication, combined with an infectious and bubbly personality, has made a big impression at Carrington. It has also caught the attention of Carrick, who wanted Lacey around the first team this season because he believed it could be a breakthrough year for the youngster.

After his impressive performance off the bench against Roma, I do not think it is getting carried away to suggest Lacey should start against Aston Villa on Sunday.

United are short of attacking options, with Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford both sidelined through injury, while Amad Diallo has looked short of confidence in front of goal.

Lacey is not the only young player who will take confidence from Tuesday night. Despite particularly strong performances from Harry Maguire and Youri Tielemans, Carrick will also be encouraged by the way his younger players rose to the challenge.

Leny Yoro continues to build on an encouraging season, while Kobbie Mainoo played a huge part in driving United forward against Roma in his first start since the beginning of October, having recovered from injury.

Throughout his time as United head coach, Carrick has largely relied on the tried and tested. He has favoured Lisandro Martinez and Maguire as his first-choice centre-back pairing over Yoro and Ayden Heaven. Matthijs de Ligt's return from a back injury could also influence those decisions.

At left-back, Carrick has used four different players in the position rather than turn to Harry Amass, the only other natural left-back in the squad besides Luke Shaw. Amass has so far been restricted to brief cameos against Sabah and Como.

Perhaps Lacey's performance on Tuesday night will encourage Carrick to put greater faith in the younger members of his squad, despite the difficult position United find themselves in this season.

These may seem like relatively small positives for an underperforming side, but the win over Roma felt like it could be a significant moment for United.

Perhaps I am being too optimistic, and the opportunity to secure Carrick's long-term future at Old Trafford has already passed. But there are signs that he has some of the ingredients to lead an unlikely revival of United's season.

The challenge now is to build on that second-half performance against Roma when they face Aston Villa on Sunday, live on Sky.

One thing, however, is clear: Lacey deserves a starring role from the start.

articles.title: Cole Palmer omission a statement by Thomas Tuchel as Ben White recalled despite boos - England squad talking points
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the Nations League games with Croatia and Spain this month, so what are the key talking points? Cole Palmer's omission dominates as the Three Lions boss favours fresh favours
articles.body:
They host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday November 12 before going to Madrid to take on world champions Spain on November 15 and Thomas Tuchel has made some big calls in his squad .

Palmer exclusion a statement from Tuchel

Cole Palmer is fit. He's in form. So, this is a statement exclusion from England boss Thomas Tuchel. An emphatic message to Palmer and other players about what is required to earn a spot in this group and stay there.

"We trust the team who was with us and had such an excellent camp [last time]," said Tuchel, when announcing his squad. "If you're in camp, if you're good and the team is flying you have every right to stay with us. You contributed in the right manner, in an excellent way."

Palmer has missed too many opportunities to do just that, Tuchel said in September, when the Chelsea ace frustratingly withdrew from international duty with injury. Palmer has been unavailable for selection because of injury three times since Tuchel took over, and he has withdrawn from a further two squads.

England checked on his fitness on the eve of this latest squad announcement and the indication was Palmer - who has started every Premier League game this season - is ready to go again this weekend.

Tuchel has options in the attacking areas Palmer likes to occupy. There are alternatives. But there's no doubt Palmer is among the most talented of the lot. But with this decision, Tuchel has shown he is willing to prioritise 'the brotherhood', as he puts it, that has been built by the England regulars.

Can Palmer break into that club? His only option is to keep fit and keep performing at the level he's shown so far this season and hope that is enough in March. For now, he's on the outside. Peter Smith

Does Mainoo need to mend fences with Tuchel?

Thomas Tuchel’s trust isn’t easy to earn, and Kobbie Mainoo may have done himself no favours in that department.

Mainoo had been promised more game time during the last camp after Tuchel’s admission that he was wrong not to give him any World Cup minutes. Then, the midfielder pulled out through injury.

He has since returned for Manchester United against Chelsea before playing 90 minutes against Roma, suggesting fitness wasn’t an issue this time around.

With Jobe Bellingham, competition in midfield is getting tougher. Whether it was his World Cup training efforts, pulling out of the last camp or a bit of both, Mainoo looks to have some bridges to rebuild if he holds out any hope for Euro 2028. Callum Bishop

Shortly after the squad was announced, Man City manager Enzo Maresca spoke in his press conference about Phil Foden's omission. "The reason why he has been left out of the international team, I don't know, but we are happy with Phil," he said.

Given his club form, it's a fair point. Across the Premier League, Champions League and Carabao Cup, the 26-year-old has four goals and four assists in 11 appearances.

But for England, whether he plays on the left, the right or as a No 10, Foden has consistently struggled to deliver.

In his last 23 appearances for his country, he has scored once, in a 3-1 friendly win over Scotland in September 2023. Across his last 34, he has provided only four assists.

By the time the next squad is announced for the March internationals, it will have been one year since Foden's last cap - and others will have seized their chance by then. Dan Long

Jobe's maturity in Germany earns his chance

Jobe Bellingham's performance in last weekend's Der Klassiker alone will not have earned him his England spot but may have sealed Thomas Tuchel's thinking that he was ready for the opportunity.

Bellingham has had to fight off inevitable comparisons to his brother in the Bundesliga and found his first season at Borussia Dortmund tough going, but two assists in eight games this season in a more advanced role since Joey Veerman's summer arrival has freed him up to do what he does best.

He may be thrown from the frying pan into the fire given Myles Lewis-Skelly's suspension, Alex Scott's injury and Kobbie Mainoo's absence, putting him back under the microscope of further sibling scrutiny as, potentially, one of the first brothers to play together for England in 30 years.

But given Jobe's composure in the pressure cooker of Germany's biggest game, and his adaptation to life in Germany, there are promising signs that he is ready to handle it. Ron Walker

Ben White's England career looked over during his self-imposed exile following a falling-out with the coaching staff at the 2022 World Cup but his call-up shows his value to Thomas Tuchel.

His return to the fold in March was divisive. He was booed by some fans at Wembley against Uruguay, even when scoring the opening goal, and again against Japan.

But Tuchel is undeterred by the acrimony, more interested in White's form since the injuries that caused him to miss the World Cup and the last camp in September.

White has impressed for Arsenal, showing the threat he offers at right-back with three assists in seven league games. He has work to do to win over England's fanbase but Tuchel is clearly an admirer. Nick Wright

Josh King's call-up follows a strong start to the season with Fulham. The 19-year-old has started every Premier League game under Alvaro Arbeloa and impressed in tough circumstances.

King, a regular in England's youth teams, has usurped club-record signing Emile Smith Rowe in the No 10 role for Fulham. It is a statement of Thomas Tuchel's belief in his ability that he has been picked ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden.

King joined England's pre-World Cup training camp and has continued to grow in stature for Fulham this season, taking on more responsibility even at his young age.

He has two goals and an assist in the Premier League so far this season and his attacking threat is evidenced by an unmatched total of 57 touches in the opposition box, which puts him ahead of Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku. Nick Wright

England face their final two Nations League A3 games this month, knowing a point against Croatia will seal a place in the competition's quarter-finals.

England vs Croatia - Thursday, November 12

articles.title: La lista de Luis de la Fuente, en directo | Última hora de la convocatoria de la Selección Española hoy, en vivo
articles.summary: Acaba la rueda de prensa de David Gordo. David Gordo: Nos vamos a decantar por el que nos transmita que pueda ayudar en el partido. Y por qué no los?
articles.body:
La lista de Luis de la Fuente, en directo | Última hora de la selección española hoy, en vivo

La segunda lista de Luis de la Fuente llega marcada por una nueva transición y por dos exigentes compromisos que servirán para medir el alcance de la renovación de la campeona continental. España afrontará esta ventana internacional con duelos de máxima exigencia ante selecciones de primer nivel, un escenario ideal para comprobar el encaje de las nuevas caras, la respuesta de los menos habituales y el estado real de un equipo que sigue buscando mantener su identidad ganadora sin renunciar a la necesaria regeneración de la plantilla.

Para esta ventana internacional llegan dos pruebas de máximo nivel en el horizonte. Con la clasificación para los cuartos de final de la UEFA Nations League ya asegurada, España visitará a República Checa en Praga el próximo día 12 de noviembre , antes de cerrar la fase de grupos frente a Inglaterra en el Metropolitano el domingo día 15. Dos encuentros de exigencia creciente que servirán para calibrar el estado de una selección en plena renovación y comprobar el peso de las novedades introducidas por el seleccionador riojano.

articles.title: Championship preview: Contenders, pretenders and strugglers
articles.summary: BBC Sport highlights five things to look out for across Saturday's Championship action.
articles.body:
With League One and League Two clubs involved in the FA Cup this weekend, the Championship has a free run of the EFL.

So far England's second tier has served up its usual helping of drama and chaos in equal measure while sacking season seems to be in full swing.

Struggling Derby County open proceedings on Friday against Bolton Wanderers and we have picked out five things you may want to keep an eye out for on Saturday.

Tom Wagner and his Knighthead Capital Management hardly made an auspicious start as owners of Birmingham City.

Sacking boss John Eustace when they were sixth in the Championship and appointing Wayne Rooney took many by surprise and, with the former Manchester United and England striker winning only two of his 15 league games in charge before being replaced by Gary Rowett, relegation became a near certainty.

A rebuild under Chris Davies saw Blues pay a League One record fee to sign Jay Stansfield, with his 19 goals helping to fire them to a record-breaking promotion.

Last season brought consolidation and a 10th-place finish with the hope for a promotion tilt this time around and the early signs are promising.

A run of five wins from their past six games has propelled Davies' side up to third, and a chance to possibly go top by beating Swansea on Saturday (15:00 GMT).

"The league table is temporary at the moment and when I came in two-and-a-half years ago we'd just been relegated, so we've come a long way and we feel like we deserve to be where we are," said Davies after Tuesday's 3-0 win over Millwall.

Swansea's visit not only provides a good test for Birmingham's credentials but also of the Welshmen's powers of recovery.

A 4-0 thrashing of Blackburn last weekend was sandwiched in between a 5-0 walloping by QPR and Tuesday's 3-1 reverse at Portsmouth which has seen Vitor Matos' side fall out of the automatic promotion places.

This then feels like a first real test for both teams to prove their worth.

Can the Hammers end a hectic week on a high?

A week is a long time in football, just ask West Ham United fans.

From the boos and jeers following a home defeat by West Brom last Saturday came the sacking of boss Nuno Espirito Santo, the appointment of Scott Parker and a crazy 3-3 draw at Cardiff City - such is the life of a Hammers supporter.

Parker is back at the club he served for four years as a player, bringing with him a reputation as a man who knows how to get teams out of the Championship. The 46-year-old has already won promotion with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley.

"I've been in this division three times and I've got out of this division three times. This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it," Parker said.

"I will use every ounce of my experience, every ounce of my knowledge, to have an understanding of what we're going to need to bring consistency."

The first 45 minutes of his tenure was a perfect example of the task facing him as the Hammers went 3-0 down at Cardiff before fighting back to claim an unlikely point.

Saturday's trip to Blackburn (15:00 GMT) brings them up against a side who have lost two on the bounce but have a habit of producing a result just when you think they are on the slide.

Chopping block for Charlton's Jones at Blades?

Now, unless you are a Sheffield United supporter you may not have noticed them so far this season but there they are, quietly going about their business in ninth place.

With four wins from their past six games the Blades have tip-toed their way into the play-off frame and only five points short of the top two.

"I'm not getting carried away, we needed to get to the first international break and work a few things out which we've done - I want to build something here and some stuff works and some doesn't so we're learning on the job," head coach Chris Wilder said after Tuesday's Sydie Peck - inspired win at Preston.

Contrast Sheffield United's emotions with those of Charlton for whom second-season syndrome is snapping at their heels.

From the highs of being top of the table after three successive wins to start the season, the Addicks have plunged to four straight defeats with no victory since the end of August.

Suddenly Saturday's meeting at The Valley (15:00 GMT) has a lot riding on it for both teams.

Life not so great for Alexander at Preston

When Graham Alexander returned to the scene of past glories as a player to become Preston North End manager towards the end of September his new team were second from bottom, three points short of the safety line.

Six games into his tenure they are now nine points adrift with a solitary draw to show for their efforts. If he had any doubt as to the size of the job he had taken on, the half-a-dozen matches since will have opened his eyes fully.

"I wanted it to be a fresh start when I came in but they're carrying baggage of the past and I can understand that, and it's my job and the coaching staff to get them to put that down and see the rest of the season as an opportunity," Alexander told BBC Radio Lancashire.

If you were looking for a team who might be carrying baggage then Southampton would have been one given the fallout from Spygate, but Saints' season has been sailing along.

Their two hiccups have come away from home, but having taken seven points from their past nine on the road they will surely be feeling confident before their trip to Deepdale (15:00 GMT).

Throughout a rather tempestuous 2025-26 season, the one constant at West Bromwich Albion was James Morrison.

Having worked their way through Ryan Mason and Eric Ramsay, Morrison was called upon to take the reins before being handed the role permanently in April as reward for steering them clear of relegation.

A five-game unbeaten run, including impressive wins over Wrexham, Blackburn and West Ham has pushed Albion into the top six going into Saturday's meeting with Millwall at The Hawthorns (15:00 GMT).

A lengthy injury list has so far prevented the Londoners from replicating last season's form which took them to the brink of automatic promotion before play-off heartbreak.

These two are seeking to be contenders for at least a top-eight finish and a result for either may show us who is the real deal and who might just be a pretender.

BBC Sport will have live text coverage of all the weekend's Championship action starting on Friday with Derby County v Bolton Wanderers (20:00 GMT).

articles.title: AFE espera que la Federación estime su petición de aplazar la jornada de Segunda
articles.standfirst: La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles espera pueda suspenderse en señal de respeto tras el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel
articles.summary: La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles espera pueda suspenderse en señal de respeto tras el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel
articles.body: La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles (AFE) espera que el Juez Único de Competiciones Profesionales de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) tenga en consideración la petición que le ha trasladado para aplazar la próxima jornada de Segunda división y las circunstancias que la motivan. El sindicato remitió una carta al juez de la RFEF, después de mantener conversaciones con todos los capitanes de los equipos de Segunda División, en la que solicitó el aplazamiento, después de la muerte del jugador del Tenerife Jesús de Miguel y su entierro ayer en la localidad toledana de Navahermosa. AFE planteó primero que se suspendiera toda la jornada y posteriormente sólo los partidos de la Segunda, petición que "responde al sentir mayoritario de los futbolistas de la categoría, que consideran que, por respeto, solidaridad y compañerismo hacia Jesús de Miguel, no debería disputarse la jornada en las actuales circunstancias". "La gran mayoría de los capitanes y de los jugadores consultados por AFE han trasladado su preocupación y malestar por esta situación, mostrando su apoyo y solidaridad hacia Jesús de Miguel, compañero de categoría. Los futbolistas entienden que este momento requiere de empatía y humanidad", afirmó en un comunicado. AFE espera por ello que el Juez Único de Competiciones Profesionales "tenga en consideración la petición trasladada y las circunstancias que la motivan". "AFE considera que en este tipo de situaciones, el fútbol debe actuar con sensibilidad con las personas que forman parte de él", insistió. El sindicato canceló todos los actos que tenía previstos esta semana en señal de duelo por la muerte este martes del jugador del Tenerife Jesús de Miguel, vocal de su junta directiva, tras el fuerte impacto que sufrió con el portero del Andorra Jesús Owono, en el minuto 96 del partido de la última jornada entre ambos, el pasado día 2 en Santa Cruz de Tenerife. La RFEF, LaLiga y Liga F rendirán un homenaje al jugador con varios actos bajo el lema 'Siempre en nuestro recuerdo', como un parón en el minuto 9 de todos los encuentros que se disputen este fin de semana, en referencia al dorsal que portaba en su camiseta, que irá acompañada por la reproducción de un vídeo en los videomarcadores de los respectivos estadios. Antes, los futbolistas titulares de ambos equipos saldrán al terreno de juego entremezclados y vistiendo una camiseta especial con el dorsal 9 y el lema 'Siempre en nuestro recuerdo'.

articles.title: Mourinho: "¿Vinicius? Nunca voy a perjudicar al equipo para beneficiar a un jugador..."
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués atendió a la prensa en la previa del partido frente al Valencia
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués atendió a la prensa en la previa del partido frente al Valencia
articles.body: José Mourinho volvió a tomar la palabra en la sala de prensa de la Ciudad Real Madrid, la última vez antes del parón de selecciones. En la previa del partido frente al Valencia, el entrenador portugués tocó todos los puntos de interés de la actualidad blanca, una que pasa por Vinicius, Valverde, descanso de sus jugadores, antes de dejar una bonita reflexión sobre si se debería suspender la jornada en honor a Jesús de Miguel: "Si fuera posible hablar con Jesús y hacerle la pregunta, sería la situación ideal. Al no ser posible. solo su familia y sus compañeros pueden responder sobre qué le gustaría que pasara". Antes, Mourinho volvió a explicar sus sensaciones con el descanso... y su queja a los horarios. Del viaje a Atenas, el club blanco aterrizó en Madrid a las 3am y todos, jugadores y cuerpo técnico, se quedaron en Valdebebas para tratar de descansar algo más. Buen momento: "Yo creo que bien, hemos llegado aquí a las 3am (viaje Atenas)... pero nos hemos quedado, ningún jugador se ha ido a casa para intentar tener un par de horas más de sueño. El feedback de los jugadores es positivo, pero no vamos ahora a dramatizar y mañana estaremos". Cristiano: "No quiero valorar más que comentar, se debe respetar y obviamente respeto esta decisión. No es una retirada, quien lo conoce sabe que tiene todavía objetivos para su carrera y la única cosa que me gustaría decir es que su retirada como jugador de fútbol, cuando llegue ese día, que sea un día diferente al día de ayer. ¿Si lo veo como entrenador? No sé lo que puede pasar por su cabeza, pero es pronto" Valverde y el brazalete: "yo no puedo comparar con el Valverde de la temporada pasada, he visto un chico profesional, humilde, amigo de sus compañeros... es un chico que está ahí de ejemplo para todos. Ser capitán del Real Madrid no es algo fácil". Mestalla: "No soy mucho de echar de menos cosas. Más que Mestalla, yo miro al Valencia como club. Lo más importante es el partido de mañana, el cual considero uno de los más difíciles de toda la Liga. Un entrenador que es muy difícil, con mucha experiencia vivida y que sabe perfectamente la filosofía que quiere para sus equipos. Será un partido difícil para nosotros. Para ganar hay que estar a tope". Atlético-Barcelona: "Me gustaría que perdiesen los dos, pero no es posible. Es fácil porque uno de los dos va a perder puntos, este fin de semana sabemos que van a quedar puntos perdidos... y te digo, con toda la honestidad, me da igual lo que pase". Suspender jornada: "Según he sido informado se van a realizar homenajes bonitos en todas las competiciones... pero de todos los modos, si fuera posible hablar con Jesús y hacerle la pregunta sería lo ideal, pero al ser imposible, sólo su familia y compañeros pueden responder que le gustaría a Jesús que pasara. Si le gustaría ser recordado con un homenaje trasversal de todas las categorías del fútbol español, es un cosa para familia y amigos... nosotros no podemos. El homenaje es a Jesús, así que tiene que hablar quien le conoce profundamente". Plan de descansos especial: "No pienso en eso. Es fácil de entender que mañana jugarán Konaté y Dean. Repartiremos minutos con los jugadores que se puede. Pero ahora, gracias a la decisión de que jugamos el sábado, los jugadores que van con su selección tienen libre el domingo". Opciones con Vinicius: "Para mí lo más importante es el equipo, nunca por voluntad propia he querido perjudicar al equipo para beneficiar un jugador. En Champions se ha podido poner esa cuestión y nada, cuando volvamos a la normalidad de Vinicius estar disponible haré mi gestión. Yo como entrenador no pienso partido a partido, pienso también en el próximo y en la secuencia que tenemos. Este último era partido para Vini, para dar descanso a jugadores como Arda que tenía algún problema... pero yo tengo que hacer todo para tener a mis jugadores al máximo nivel. Creer siempre en el verdadero potencial del jugador, un jugador malo será siempre malo por mucho que intentes... y un jugador buen, en sus momentos malos, te deja la puerta abierta a que pueda volver a su situación normal. Si llega a ser otro jugador y no Vinicius el partido de Atenas se hubiera dicho que era un partido normal. El Vinicius del año pasado me eliminó de Champions y no queda otra que continuar trabajando. La amistad de sus compañeros, todos sin excepción, y vamos con todo y toda la creencia, pero a la hora de la verdad, que es la hora de decidir, el equipo tiene que estar por encima de cualquier jugador". Racha positiva... y parón: "Me da miedo el partido de mañana, miedo entre comillas. La dificultad del partido de mañana es mi prioridad, la selección no veo que sea un problema si respetan a los jugadores: minutos, cuidado... no me preocupa nada que un jugador tenga el honor de ir a jugar con su país. La prioridad es contra un partido que tiene a sus jugadores frescos, contra un entrenador que no está preocupado en si tiene que jugar maravillosamente bien, sólo está pensando en ganar". ¿En qué fase se encuentra el equipo?: "Es mejor no remontar, es mejor como en Santander con 0-3 al descanso. Remontar significa cosa positiva, pero también negativa. Es la creencia, un banquillo rico, motivación del grupo, es el saber que camiseta tienes... pero también su parte negativa y ese lado tenemos que trabajarlo. Encontrar más uniformidad a la hora de empezar los partidos".

articles.title: England squad: Cole Palmer, Phil Foden and Kobbie Mainoo left out as Jobe Bellingham and Josh King called up
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel names his 25-man England squad for Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain; Cole Palmer, Phil Foden, Kobbie Mainoo left out; Jobe Bellingham and Josh King handed first senior call-ups; Ben White and Djed Spence return; Bukayo Saka, Adam Scott, Marcus Rashford injured
articles.body:
Chelsea's Palmer was hugely disappointed when he was overlooked for the World Cup in the summer after a stop-start season due to injury, and he withdrew from the last England camp in September and October because of a minor fitness issue, but he has been back to his best this season with five goals and three assists in 11 appearances.

England made medical checks with Chelsea on Thursday over Palmer and Sky Sports News understands those checks confirmed he was fully fit and ready to take a full part in England's upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

Speaking about Palmer's omission on Friday, Tuchel said the "door is always open" for him and added: "I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, Cole is no exception. It counts when you're in camp. I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. The players who were in camp built something extraordinary.

"It's not personal. We'll never assume Cole isn't in the mindset to come and play for his country but the competition is on and the players in the [last] camp did an amazing job."

Manchester United midfielder Mainoo also withdrew from the previous squad with an unspecified injury having failed to feature at the World Cup despite being selected.

Tuchel stressed the importance of attending England squads when called up and believes the message is landing.

He said: "It's always the ones who are in camp, the ones who don't withdraw, the ones who walk the talk, and come to camp and show it matters and put the quality in. That's what we will always reward.

"I think it's naturally coming through, without needing to talk about it. That was always the message since very early since we took charge: it matters when you're in camp.

"It matters what you do in camp. The last camp was an excellent one, so the trust and belief is on the players who were there."

Manchester City forward Foden remains out of favour despite contributing six goal involvements in as many games, having been overlooked for last summer's tournament and the autumn squad.

However, the notable absences have created opportunities for first-time call-ups for King and Borussia Dortmund's Jobe Bellingham, both of whom have previously represented England at youth level.

Defenders Trevoh Chalobah and Tino Livramento have both withdrawn through injury, while left-back Nico O'Reilly misses out after being deemed "not 100 per cent" by Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca, but Real Madrid right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold retains his place in the squad.

Inter Milan full-back Djed Spence returns for the first time since the World Cup after an injury, while Arsenal defender Ben White is recalled after being overlooked since March, when some England supporters booed him .

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is ruled out with a thigh injury, so Everton's James Garner , who was called up as a replacement in the autumn, comes in.

Nottingham Forest forward Morgan Gibbs-White and Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha will look to fill the void left by injured England stalwarts Marcus Rashford and Bukayo Saka , with Arsenal winger Noni Madueke overlooked.

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton & Hove Albion), James Trafford (Leeds United)

Defenders: Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Marc Guehi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Ben White (Arsenal).

Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), James Garner (Everton), Josh King (Fulham), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal).

Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea).

Thursday November 12: England vs Croatia, 7.45pm kick-off

Sunday November 15: Spain vs England, 7.45pm kick-off

Tuchel sends out clear message with Palmer decision

"In leaving Cole Palmer out of this squad, Thomas Tuchel has sent a clear message to both the Chelsea man, and to every other England wannabe, whatever your status and experience in international football.

"The message is stark - you have to be present, you have to be committed, you have to be humble, as part of a wider push for a positive squad dynamic. And for Tuchel, it is clear he feels Palmer has not done enough to prove he has those three qualities. Tuchel doesn't doubt his ability - eight goal involvements in 11 matches is a much better output than either Ebe Eze or Morgan Gibbs-White have managed so far this season. And yet they are both in, and Palmer is out.

"When he withdrew from the last England squad in September because of a minor injury, that was the final straw for Tuchel. Five times, since the German coach took over in January 2025, Palmer has been unavailable because of injury. On two of those occasions, Tuchel named Palmer in his squad, only for him to withdraw. He has only played three matches in the Tuchel era.

"If he had picked Palmer this time, and dropped another number 10 to accommodate him, that would have been entirely the wrong message that Tuchel wanted to portray to the rest of his squad.

"Tuchel expects the sort of loyalty and determination shown by John Stones, Jude Bellingham and - most recently - Declan Rice, who have all chosen to still spend some time with the squad, even when they weren't fit enough to play.

"So, the England boss has made an example of the man who scored for his country in a Euros final two years ago. And that should be taken as a warning to Palmer personally, and as a cautionary tale to everyone else who wants to be part of his England squad."

" Josh King's England call-up follows a strong start to the season with Fulham. The 19-year-old, who made his senior breakthrough under Marco Silva, has started every Premier League game under Alvaro Arbeloa and impressed in tough circumstances.

"King, a regular in England's youth teams, has usurped club-record signing Emile Smith Rowe in the No 10 role for Fulham. It is a testament to Thomas Tuchel's belief in his ability that he sees him as an option in a position in which England are stacked with talent. King has been picked ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden. It is a statement by the manager.

"King joined England's pre-World Cup training camp and only narrowly missed out on selection for September's squad, according to Tuchel. Since then, he has continued to grow in stature for Fulham, taking on more responsibility even at his young age.

"He has two goals and an assist in the Premier League so far this season and his attacking threat is evidenced by an unmatched total of 57 touches in the opposition box, which puts him ahead of Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku. Now to test himself with England."

"Ben White's England career appeared to be over during his self-imposed exile following a fall-out with Gareth Southgate and Steve Holland at the 2022 World Cup but the Arsenal defender's call-up underlines his value to Thomas Tuchel.

"White's return to the fold in March was divisive. He was booed by some fans at Wembley against Uruguay, even when scoring the opening goal, and ended up conceding a late penalty before attracting more boos in the subsequent meeting with Japan.

"But Tuchel may well have included him in his World Cup squad if not for the knee injury he suffered in May and clearly the manager has not been put off by the hamstring issue that caused him to miss England's last camp in September.

"White has impressed for Arsenal this season, starting regularly at right-back with Jurrien Timber sidelined for the opening months of the campaign. He has shown the attacking threat he offers in the role with three assists in seven Premier League appearances.

"His versatility, as a natural centre-back, likely adds to his appeal to Tuchel but his reception in March shows he still has work to do to repair relations with the Three Lions fanbase."

articles.title: Conor Coady: Former Wolves, Everton, Leicester defender retires at the age of 33
articles.summary: Coady started out at boyhood club Liverpool and went on to play for Sheffield United, Huddersfield, Wolves, Everton, Leicester, Wrexham and Charlton; the defender also earned 10 senior England caps between 2020 and 2022
articles.body:
The defender revealed the news in a post on Instagram on Friday morning, captioned: "Lived the dream. Eternally Grateful, Thank you."

Coady left Wrexham on August 31, when his contract was terminated by mutual consent.

His final game came on May 2, when he played 61 minutes of a 3-1 defeat to Swansea, during a loan spell at Charlton.

The news comes after an announcement on Thursday that he would co-host ' The Football Dugout' - a new weekly podcast and YouTube show alongside Sky Sports football presenter, Mark Chapman.

During a career that spanned 15 years, Coady also played for boyhood club Liverpool, Sheffield United, Huddersfield, Everton and Leicester.

He spent more than half of that time at Wolves, making 317 appearances for the club in all competitions.

After winning the Championship title in 2017/18, Coady missed just one Premier League game across the next four seasons at Molineux.

Between 2020 and 2022, he earned 10 senior caps for England and was part of both the Euro 2020 and World Cup 2022 squads, though he did not play at either tournament.

After coaching both England U19 and U21 sides earlier this year, Coady revealed in September that he had returned to Liverpool.

"I'm trying to keep myself busy," he told BBC Radio 5 Live Sport .

"I'm lucky enough to get the opportunity to go into Liverpool's U21s. I came through there. I'm doing a little bit of coaching with the boys, which has been brilliant.

"The lads at Liverpool are amazing with me. The players but also Jay Spearing and Rob Page, who gave me the opportunity to come in, mirror them a little bit, be in the office before training and look at how they plan a session.

"If they need numbers, I'll jump in and keep myself fit as well. That's what it's looking like at the minute."

articles.summary: Jude Bellingham, Trent y Gordon están en la lista para los compromisos ante Croacia y España; Palmer se vuelve a quedar fuera
articles.body: Inglaterra ha hecho pública este viernes la lista de jugadores convocados para los dos partidos de la Nations League ante Croacia y España. Ngumoha, King, Calvert-Lewin junto a Gibbs-White son novedades de Tuchel para estos dos compromisos, pero la principal novedad es la de Jobe Bellingham, hermano del madridista, que se estrena en una convocatoria. Tuchel, el seleccionador, vuelve a dejar fuera a Cole Palmer. El jugador del Chelsea se había hecho chequeos médicos para dejar claro que está listo para jugar, pero el entrenador ha decidido volver a dejarle fuera de la convocatoria, agrandando una crisis que se remonta a antes del Mundial. Otros que se han quedado fuera son Rashford y Saka. Por contra, Bellingham y Trent, jugadores del Real Madrid, forman parte de la lista. También Anthony Gordon, cuyo rendimiento en el Barcelona está siendo bueno.

articles.title: ‘I needed him by my side’: Jorge Jesus reveals he urged Ronaldo to stay after rift led to Portugal retirement decision
articles.summary: Jorge Jesus reveals he urged Cristiano Ronaldo to remain with the national team following the forward's decision to retire from international football after a rift. The coach speaks of Ronaldo's pivotal role in Portugal's football history and a tribute at the Portuguese Football Federation.
articles.body: Jorge Jesus wanted Cristiano Ronaldo to remain part of Portugal’s plans, but the national team coach has accepted that he could not persuade the forward to reverse his decision. Speaking after Ronaldo announced his international retirement on Thursday, November 5, Jesus revealed that he had personally asked the 41-year-old to continue representing his country, while also confirming that a photograph of the former captain had been installed at the Portuguese Football Federation’s headquarters as a tribute to his contribution.Jorge Jesus asked Ronaldo to stay with PortugalJesus admitted that he had hoped to retain Ronaldo in the Portugal squad, having worked with the forward for a year at Al Nassr before taking charge of the national team. Speaking to Portuguese broadcaster Canal 11, the coach said he had made his position clear before announcing his first squad, telling Ronaldo that he wanted him involved regardless of whether he was selected to play."We had the opportunity to speak before the first call-up. I asked him to continue with me because I needed him by my side. But I have to accept his decision," Jesus said.The coach also described Ronaldo as an important figure in Portugal's football history and a role model for younger generations, recognising the influence he has had beyond his performances for the national team."He will always be a reference for our national team, our people and our history," Jesus added.In a further tribute, Jesus said he had arranged for a large photograph of Ronaldo to be displayed in the auditorium of the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF). He wanted the image to remain visible to young players, colleagues and others using the facility, ensuring that the former captain's contribution would remain part of the environment in which future generations of Portuguese footballers develop.The FPF has also expressed its intention to organise a farewell ceremony in recognition of Ronaldo's service. Its official statement described him as an inspirational leader and the eternal captain, although the details of the proposed event have not yet been finalised.What led to Ronaldo's retirement from Portugal?Ronaldo's announcement followed a difficult period involving his relationship with Jesus, with reports in Portugal pointing to disagreements during the September and October international breaks.The reported tension began after Ronaldo was left on the bench against Norway and subsequently learned that he would not start Portugal's next match against Denmark. He then left the national team's training camp, an incident that reportedly prompted disciplinary action from the FPF. The forward received a 30-day suspension and a fine following the episode. Despite the strained relationship, Ronaldo was included in Portugal's preliminary squad for the November international break, with the team scheduled to face Denmark and WalesJesus had previously insisted that Ronaldo remained welcome in the squad and had made clear that the decision about his international future belonged to the player. In comments last month, he reiterated that position."Cristiano should end his time in the national team the way he wants, he's the one who will decide how he wants it. In my first call-up, I said, 'I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you'. And now I'm saying the same thing."Reports also suggested that Ronaldo had informed FPF president Pedro Proença of his decision before making it public, without first discussing it with Jesus. The coach's latest comments make clear that he wanted the forward to stay, even as he acknowledged that the final choice was not his to make.Portugal are due to face Denmark and Wales during the November international break, with Ronaldo's retirement bringing his involvement with the senior national team to an end.Ronaldo leaves Portugal with 146 goals and two major recordsRonaldo's departure closes a 23-year international career that began with his senior debut in August 2003. He finishes as the leading goalscorer in men's international football, with 146 goals in 234 appearances, and holds Portugal's record for the most caps.His greatest team achievement came at Euro 2016, when he captained Portugal to their first major international title. He later helped the country win the Nations League in 2019 and again in 2025.Ronaldo also became the first men's player to score at six different FIFA World Cups, extending that record at the 2026 tournament. His international career combined individual scoring records with a period in which Portugal established itself among the leading teams in European football.His international retirement, however, does not end his club career. He remains with Al Nassr, while his son continues to work towards establishing himself in Portugal's youth teams.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: LaLiga denuncia insultos a Oscar Puente y Pedro Sánchez en Getafe, Santander y Elche
articles.summary: LaLiga incluyó en su escrito de denuncias por incidentes en la undécima jornada de LaLiga EA Sports insultos al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, y al exministro de Transportes Óscar Puente en los estadios del Getafe, el Racing de Santander y el Elche.
articles.body: LaLiga incluyó en su escrito de denuncias por incidentes en la undécima jornada de LaLiga EA Sports insultos al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, y al exministro de Transportes Óscar Puente en los estadios del Getafe, el Racing de Santander y el Elche. El escrito que LaLiga remite semanalmente al Comité de Disciplina de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) y a la Comisión Antiviolencia refleja que, antes del inicio del partido Getafe-Sevilla, un grupo de aficionados locales entonaron el cántico "Óscar Puente, asesino", que también se escuchó antes de empezar el encuentro Elche-Valencia. La denuncia de LaLiga reprodujo que un minuto antes del inicio del Racing-Real Madrid aficionados locales entonaron el cántico "Pedro Sánchez, hijo de puta" y también que durante el mismo hubo insultos hacia el Real Madrid. El cántico "¡Arriba, arriba, arriba, arriba, arriba con la Goma-2, que en Vallecas se prepara, que en Vallecas se prepara ¡PIM PAM PUM! la revolución!", entonado por aficionados del Rayo Vallecano frente al Celta de Vigo también figura en el escrito, junto a insultos de seguidores del Getafe hacia el Sevilla y el Leganés y del Albacete al Sabadell, en la duodécima jornada de LaLiga Hypermotion. LaLiga, que solicita desde hace años más competencias para luchar contra la violencia en los estadios, recoge, a través de su plataforma LALIGAVS, los reportes, sugerencias o requerimientos de los aficionados que acudan a los partidos para contribuir a ello.
