articles.title: Terzic tira de De Marcos para encarar la visita de este sábado a Osasuna
articles.standfirst: Paredes es baja, Galarreta vuelve y hay dudas con la disponibilidad de Nico Serrano y Djaló
articles.summary: Paredes es baja, Galarreta vuelve y hay dudas con la disponibilidad de Nico Serrano y Djaló
articles.body: El Athletic realizará esta tarde un último entrenamiento para encarar el duelo de este sábado ante Osasuna. Edin Terzic se ha apoyado en De Marcos, uno de los asistentes en el primer equipo, para preparar un encuentro de máxima intensidad. “Será un derbi lleno de emociones, nos hemos preparado bien y sabemos cómo juegan con Arrasate. De Marcos nos ha dado mucha visión sobre este equipo. No hay muchos goles en los partidos recientes y nos preparamos para algo similar, será caliente el ambiente. Debemos ser constantes y efectivos, además de estar enchufados”, destacó. El preparador rojiblanco recupera a Galarreta, pero descartó a Paredes, que volverá tras el parón. También dijo que esperará al entrenamiento vespertino para decidir qué pasará con Nico Serrano y Djaló. “Nico tuvo un dolor muscular tras la Copa y Álvaro ha empezado a entrenar, pero le dieron una patada en la pierna y no pudo andar por dolor. Esperamos que uno de los dos esté disponible para mañana ”, resaltó. En el análisis de la plantilla también destacó el paso adelante de Hugo Rincón para jugar de titular en el lateral derecho. “ Ha jugado muy bien y merece tener minutos tras sus últimas actuaciones”. El alemán considera clave para un resultado positivo superar los múltiples duelos que se producirán durante el encuentro. “Todo empieza con la mentalidad y jugadores preparados para los duelos y ganar duelos. Queremos defender muy alto, un buen posicionamiento es la base para ser agresivos en ataque. Budimir es su peligro en el balón parado, pero no se puede marcar sólo a él”, dijo. En la próxima ventana FIFA el entrenador perderá a varios futbolistas convocados por selecciones. Simón, Nico y Laporte viajarán con España; Peio Canales lo hará con la sub’21 española; Padilla con la absoluta de México e Imga afrontará el Mundial sub’17 hasta mediados de diciembre. Junto a ellos, al menos media docena de futbolistas irán convocados con Euskadi para jugar ante Venezuela. “Espero que todo el mundo vuelva a casa con buen estado en ánimo y sin lesiones. Hemos tenido lesiones tras el último parón, pero momentos increíbles como el de Unai Simón que viene de su Mundial. Para Imga es una experiencia increíble para beneficiarnos en el futuro. Es un gran cumplido como club y estamos contentos que vayan y que vengan sanos y salvo”, insiste. La jornada estará marcada por el homenaje a De Miguel, delantero del Tenerife fallecido tras un violento choque en el campo de juego con Owono, portero del Andorra. El minuto de silencio tendrá continuidad con un parón del partido en el minuto 9 para recordar al futbolista. El entrenador del Athletic se mostró favorable a todo lo que organice la Liga al respecto: “Preguntas al entrenador, pero tengo que responder como persona y como ser humano. En primer lugar , mi más sentido pésame a todos los que conocían a Jesús... que querían a Jesús, a su familia, a sus amigos y a todos sus compañeros de equipo. No hay palabras adecuadas para describir lo que ha pasado. Lo que decida la Liga al respecto lo entenderé y lo respetaré totalmente porque esto es algo más importante que el fútbol”.

articles.title: Emilio García Silvero deja la FIFA
articles.standfirst: Hasta la fecha, ocupaba el cargo de Jefe de Asuntos Jurídicos y Cumplimiento Normativo dentro de la institución internacional
articles.summary: Hasta la fecha, ocupaba el cargo de Jefe de Asuntos Jurídicos y Cumplimiento Normativo dentro de la institución internacional
articles.body: La FIFA anunció este viernes que Emilio García Silvero, director jurídico de la FIFA en los últimos ocho años, deja su puesto de Director del Departamento Legal y Cumplimiento para iniciar una nueva etapa profesional en Madrid. El fútbol español pierde así un referente en el organigrama ejecutivo en el máximo organismo que rige el fútbol mundial. A voluntad propia, Emilio García Silvero cierra un ciclo en el seno de la FIFA, una vez pasado el Mundial 2026, y en pleno desarrollo ya de la candidatura del Mundial 2030 que organizarán España, Portugal y Marruecos en 2030, con la sede de la final aún pendiente de designar. García Silvero lideró grandes cambios en aspectos de regulación del fútbol mundial, entre otros, la Cámara de Compensación de pagos internacionales, las normas de agentes de futbolistas recientemente validadas por el TJUE o el nuevo sistema de traspasos internacionales. Además, su dirección en programas globales ayudaron a que el acceso a las normas del fútbol fueran más cercanas y transparentes en las seis confederaciones de la FIFA.Durante este período, García Silvero ostentó diferentes posiciones en comisiones del COI, la Agencia Mundial Antidopaje o el TAS. La FIFA, a través de un comunicado oficial, dio las gracias a Emilio García Silvero por sus ocho años de dedicación al fútbol mundial. "Después de ocho años liderando el departamento de Legal y de Cumplimiento, Emilio García Silvero ha expresado su deseo de abordar una nueva etapa profesional y regresar a España". "Desde su llegada a FIFA en la Copa del Mundo 2018, Emilio ha realizado una activa contribución en el desarrollo y modernización del marco normativo que regula la gobernanza del fútbol internacional. En su etapa como ejecutivo, ha liderado un equipo de profesionales en las oficinas de Zurich y Miami, dirigiendo grandes proyectos y reformas regulatorias, iniciativas educativas y programas con el objetivo de reforzar la transparencia, la seguridad jurídica y el acceso al conocimiento de las normas y reglamentos del fútbol", subraya la nota. FIFA, por último, indica el texto, "expresa su agradecimiento a Emilio por su compromiso, profesionalidad y empatía a lo largo de estos años sirviendo al fútbol mundial". El secretario general, Mattias Grafström, le trasladó personalmente su mensaje de gratitud por su inquebrantable compromiso y su pasión por mejorar el fútbol. Emilio García Silvero, hasta ahora máximo responsable jurídico de la FIFA, confirmó "su regreso a casa" y dio las gracias por los más de 15 años de trabajo en el fútbol internacional en Nyon, Zurich y últimamente en la oficina de Miami. "Ha sido realmente un sueño trabajar junto a compañeros de todo el mundo por mejorar el marco normativo del fútbol internacional. Nada de esto habría sido posible sin las personas, el equipo y los compañeros de otras instituciones futbolísticas nacionales e internacionales que compartían la misma pasión y ambición: mejorar el sistema. También me gustaría dar las gracias al presidente y al secretario general de la FIFA por su confianza y apoyo a lo largo de todos estos años", apuntó. La salida de García Silvero de FIFA llega en la recta final del año 2026, y tras acabar el ciclo de mandato de su presidente Gianni Infantino, en un contexto previo a la celebración de las nuevas elecciones a la presidencia, previstas para el18 de marzo de 2027 en Rabat (Marruecos), y en donde Infantino ha recuperado el pulso para optar a la reelección con el respaldo de las Confederaciones, salvo la UEFA, que ha reiterado este año su insistente oposición.

articles.title: Liverpool: Andoni Iraola demands creativity over control to solve Premier League scoring problems
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola calls on Liverpool to sacrifice control of games in order to score more after struggles in front of goal; watch Crystal Palace vs Liverpool live on Sky Sports Main Event from 12.30pm on Sunday kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
The Reds have created the second-fewest big chances in the Premier League this season and scored only four goals in five home games, their joint-fewest at this stage of a season in their history.

They set an unwanted record against Arsenal last weekend , failing to register a shot on target in a home Premier League game for the first time in more than 440 games since Opta records began in 2003.

Iraola arrived at Anfield last summer with a reputation for front-foot, direct football but has had difficulties imposing his philosophy on his new players in the first three months of the season, and now wants them to take more risks to turn their domination into clear-cut opportunities.

He said: "Obviously, we want to score more and concede fewer. It's a matter of controlling the games but also sometimes, against Fenerbahce we were controlling the game too much.

"In possession we can have good positions, but sometimes we have to throw numbers inside the box, arrive with more players.

"It will take a little bit of control away, but it will give us more threat when we arrive. Especially against Arsenal, the way we attacked the box had to be better.

"We are one of the teams which arrives the most in the final third. In terms of volume of shots and crosses, we are very high - but if you analyse the quality level of chance, it is low.

"When we start losing games, attacking against a lot of positions, it's not going to be the quality of the chances.

"The number of times we get to the box, we have to arrive better. Even if that means losing some control, we have to get into the six-yard box more. It will give us more clear shots."

Liverpool 'too honest' after penalty shouts rejected

Liverpool's 1.05xG in Sunday's 1-0 defeat to Arsenal would have been significantly boosted had they been awarded a clear penalty for a shirt pull by Jurrien Timber on Alexander Isak.

Iraola admitted after the game he felt a spot kick would have been awarded had Isak gone to ground, and after being praised by the officials in Wednesday's Champions League defeat at Fenerbahce feels his side can be "too honest".

"We are an honest group. Too honest, sometimes," he said. "The referee congratulated us after the game on Wednesday, and I don't know if I liked that.

"It has to be genuine. You cannot fake things. When we complain, it has to be a genuine complaint.

"I feel we are willing, obviously, we're a team that wants to press and be intense. But the balance there is a big difference."

Isak has scored six of Liverpool's 11 Premier League goals this season after struggling with injury and form in his first year at Anfield.

Despite the Reds' wider goalscoring problems he sits second only to Erling Haaland in the race for the Golden Boot, leaving Iraola full of praise for the forward who has already doubled his league tally from last season.

"Alex is a top goal scorer," he said. "If we can put him more in the position to score he will deliver, that is not a guarantee but is the closest thing to a guarantee.

"Like every player, he can add more things to his game but we want to use [more] the things that he has. He is very good at attacking the space, attacking the channels, coming to receive the ball is very clean, also.

"We are trying to use Isak in the best way."

"Their shot locations help to explain the disparity. Closer-range shots typically have a higher probability of going in. Liverpool, though, have taken a large chunk of their total from long distance.

"The Reds have the fourth-highest percentage of shots from outside the box in the division at 39 per cent, behind only Manchester United, Hull and Newcastle, all of whom sit in the bottom half of the Premier League table nine games into the season.

"By contrast, Liverpool's proportion of shots from inside the six-yard box is the sixth-lowest in the division, at eight per cent.

"It is worth noting the two sides with the highest percentages of shots from inside the six-yard box are leaders Arsenal and second-placed Manchester City on 17 per cent and 13 per cent respectively."

articles.title: Eight SEC contenders. Four massive games. One Saturday that could change everything
articles.summary: The top eight teams in the SEC are all facing off against one another this weekend, all with postseason implications.
articles.body:
Cancel all your plans this weekend. If you've been invited to a wedding, skip it. They're boring anyway. If your child has a birthday, duck out on it. They'll have more. Buy three more TVs so you can watch 16 games at once. Whatever it takes, devote this weekend to college football. Everything else can wait.

In the South, the leaves are turning, there's the first hint of a chill in the air, you might hear the first holiday songs — and so what? The top eight teams in the SEC are all facing off against one another this weekend, all with postseason implications. The conference's 16 members have spent the first nine weeks of the season beating up on one another, and the result is this: a weekend with everything to play for, a weekend where no one can feel safe. Let's dive in.

Texas (6-2, No. 7 in CFP rankings) at Missouri (6-2, No. 18 in CFP rankings), noon ET

At stake for Texas: A chance to stop the slow, inexorable slide down the rankings. A win over Mizzou won't do too much for the Longhorns' playoff rankings, but a loss would put Texas in treacherous territory. That win over Ohio State is a long way away and losing luster with every week.

At stake for Missouri: Everything. If the Tigers lose this one, the chances of making the CFP dwindle to almost nothing. Even with a win, they'd still need substantial help from teams like Miami, Alabama and Kentucky to clear a path above them, and wins over Georgia and Kentucky ahead. In another conference, they'd be in the mix; in the 2026 SEC, they're fighting for scraps.

Alabama (6-2, No. 5) at LSU (6-2, No. 14), 3:30 ET

At stake for Alabama: The luckiest team in the CFP somehow has room to weather even a loss, which is good for the Tide because there's little indication this current Alabama squad is going to match up with a desperate LSU. A road win in Baton Rouge vaults Alabama into contention for yet another SEC title game; a loss makes the path rockier but still (barely) manageable, especially with no remaining ranked opponents on the Tide's slate.

At stake for LSU: A chance to get firmly back into the CFP conversation. Beating the No. 5 team buys you plenty of committee credibility and reorients a season that had been wobbling. A loss, and LSU suddenly has a massive hill to climb to even sneak in the back door of the CFP. Texas and Tennessee still remain on LSU's schedule, giving the Tigers more opportunity than most to rewrite their season late, but a loss this weekend would make the rest of the season win-or-else.

Kentucky (7-1, No. 6) at Tennessee (6-2, No. 13), 6:15 ET

What's at stake for Kentucky: The Wildcats are in rare air, in the hunt for a spot in the SEC championship and beginning CFP rankings season with, shockingly, a bit of a cushion. A road win in a loud environment further burnishes Kentucky's improbable playoff credentials and keeps one of the SEC's best stories rolling. A loss, and matters get trickier; the 'Cats must still face Missouri, Florida and Louisville without much margin for error.

What's at stake for Tennessee: Probably everything. A win would almost certainly push the Volunteers into the low edge of the playoff bracket, and from there Tennessee would just need to hold serve against its remaining opponents, including LSU, to return to the CFP. A loss, and it's probably adios, Rocky Top. Too many other three-loss teams will be in the hunt for those final playoff slots.

Georgia (7-1, No. 2) at Ole Miss (6-2, No. 10), 7:30 ET

At stake for Georgia: A potential SEC championship berth and playoff bye. Georgia has a long, long way to fall before it has to worry about its CFP berth, and one loss in Oxford to the No. 10 team won't do that. A tough road win would further solidify the Dawgs as one of the nation's best teams — and, depending on the Notre Dame-Miami outcome, a No. 1 ranking is tantalizingly within reach.

At stake for Ole Miss: A signature win over the No. 2 team keeps the Rebels in the conference title game hunt, particularly depending on what happens earlier in the day. A loss makes even a playoff berth that much more difficult, though Ole Miss' final three games are against unranked opponents. Still, they won't control their own destiny with a loss, and you never want to rely on the kindness of CFP committee members.

Here's the bottom-line conundrum for the SEC: pound for pound and team for team, the conference is as deep and stacked as it's ever been. (Auburn, the conference's 12th-ranked team, won in Athens this season.) But simple math is vexing the SEC; several of the conference's good teams will have large numbers in their loss columns, making their route into the playoff more difficult.

Wins by lower-ranked teams like LSU, Tennessee and Ole Miss could help pack the playoff bracket, but they'll also lead to quality teams watching the dance from outside. The only predictable element out of this weekend, and this season as a whole, is more unpredictability. Buckle up.

articles.title: Le Pagelle: Juventus vs. AZ Alkmaar
articles.summary: The Bianconeri made a straightforward victory anything but in the last minutes, but came through for the win.
articles.body:
After Sunday's victory against Napoli, my biggest hope was that Juventus would manage to keep some of that momentum going. It's something that Juve have tended to struggle with over the last few years, and given the side's current problems, they really couldn't afford another Brigadoon game.

(Side note: the more I've used that phrase this past week the more I like the image comparing Juve's good games to the fleeting glimpses of the titular town in the musical. I don't know if I officially coined it or not, but I'm claiming it, because why the hell not?)

Thursday night's Europa League match against AZ Alkmaar was a perfect test to see if that momentum could be kept up. AZ were a Pot 1 peer who hadn't lost a European game at home in over three years — a total of 17 consecutive games coming in — and were just three spots behind Juve in the early League Phase table. It was also a homecoming for Teun Koopmeiners, who began his career at AZ and in this match would come face-to-face with his younger brother, Peer, who has been at the AFAS Stadion his entire career.

Ironically, it was the elder Koopemeiners who got the scoring going with a neatly-taken goal in the 19th minute, followed very much against the run of play by Randal Kolo Muani 18 minutes later, produced largely by the Frenchman's sheer force of will.

But Juve were otherwise defending for long stretches against the home side. They missed a few chances to put the game away on the counter, but some shambolic defending with three minutes to go let AZ back in the game, and they very nearly squandered the lead entirely in stoppage time before being bailed out by the offside flag.

But in the end they were able to hold just enough, and fly home to Turin with a 2-1 victory that vaulted them two spots to fifth in the table, and did indeed keep the momentum going forward as they head into the final game before the international break on Sunday.

How did everyone do in this European matchup? Let's take a closer look.

GUGLIELMO VICARIO – 6. Played a good game overall, and made a pretty spectacular-looking save in stoppage time that ultimately didn't count thanks to the offside flag — and thank goodness, because the game would've been tied otherwise.

FEDERICO GATTI – 7. Had absolutely everything covered on defense until his odd withdrawal with 10 minutes to go (more on that later). He blocked three shots and made five interceptions, and the only reason this grade isn't quite a bit higher still is that he flubbed a couple of counterattacks in the second half that could've put the game fully beyond reach.

JHON LUCUMÍ – 5.5. His numbers were good — two tackles, two blocks, two interceptions, five clearances — but he got caught ballwatching on Mexx Meerdink's goal and let the striker get a few strides behind him for an easy tap-in.

LLOYD KELLY – 5.5. Docked for giving the ball away deep in the run-up to the goal. Relatively solid beside, with four clearances and a key pass going the other way.

PIERRE KALULU – 6. Blocked three shots and pressed well when he was up in attack, even if he didn't have a whole lot in the way of numbers to show for it. His presence helped cause the turnover that led to Kolo Muani's goal.

TEUN KOOPMEINERS – 7. Put aside his emotions to have a really great day. The goal he scored looked far easier than it was. The first-time side-footed shot used the pace from the cross without dissipating it in the slightest from 18 yards — it took an incredible amount of skill. He also notched a key pass and co-led the team with two dribbles, while also racking up five clearances on defense. One of his best games in a Juve shirt, if we're honest.

PAPE MATER SARR – 6.5. A powerful ball-winner in midfield. Led the team with four tackles and was one of three players that registered four clearances as well.

ANDREA CAMBIASO – 6. Nothing terrible, nothing great either. Had a pair of tackles and got a rather harsh yellow card in an early-second-half tangle that saw a lot of grabbing and pulling on both sides and ended with him on the ground.

RANDAL KOLO MUANI – 7. A goal and a assist that were both made possible by his industry and inventiveness as he played out wide on the right. Looked far more confident, almost as if getting booed off the field on Sunday struck a nerve.

KERIM ALAJBEGOVIC – 5.5. His passing was really rough (63.6 percent) and that dragged down what was otherwise a pretty passable game. Very nearly scored another fabulous goal in the first half but fired his shot just high.

NICK WOLTEMADE – 6. Played a good one-two with Kolo Muani to assist on the second goal, and led the team with three key passes overall. Could've been higher, but for the second straight game the dude didn't manage to take a shot, which is kinda important when it comes to being a striker.

JÉRÉMIE BOGA – 5.5. Made a dribble and worked hard but constantly defending over the second half.

JUAN CABAL – 5. Let Elijah Dijkstra in behind with a spectacular piece of ball-watching that allowed him to set up AZ's goal. Unfortunate that he follows up one of his best performances in years with this match.

BREMER – NR. Not sure why he was coming on, or why he replaced who he did. Had a pair of clearances but that was about it.

JEFF EKHATOR – NR. Got booked a little harshly and was barely able to sniff the ball at his feet in the box. Defended dilligentlt thought.

DOUGLAS LUIZ – NR. An attempt to solidify the midfield for the last few minutes but it didn't have the time to do much of anything.

There were definitely some major problems in Spalletti's approach on Thursday night against AZ Alkmaar, and it nearly cost them the game.

The overall attitude was reactive as opposed to proactive, which always drives me around the bend, especially for a coach who has shown the ability to put together teams that can do the latter. AZ finished the game with 56.4 percent possession, but it felt like a whole lot more than that at times. In between Juve's two goals, the number was 72.7 percent, which makes what turned out to be the deciding goal all the more remarkable.

Yes, AZ had come into the game not having fewer than 50 percent possession all year long, but leaving them to pile on pressure for long stretches was eventually going to cost the team, and it finally did when Kelly gave up possession deep and then the entire team turned in an impressive display of ball watching. Perhaps things would be different had Juve converted one of a couple of chances to make it 3-0 early in the second half, but sitting back and waiting for the game to come to them, especially with an defense that has proven itself mistake-prone, simply isn't the right way to approach things. After a good first half Juve basically stopped attacking beyond the odd counter in the second half, which completely negated a well-chosen (for what was available) lineup that got up 2-0 in spite of giving up the game's initiative.

There was also the weird decision to substitute Gatti, who had been imperious in defense up to that point and clearly one of, if not the best Juve players in the match for 80 minutes. Gatti had made a few lung-busting runs up the field on the counter as the second half had worn on, and maybe that combined with the results of those attacks led Spalletti to believe that he was gassed, but despite a good individual effort by Bremer in the last 10 minutes, it seemed to cause a little bit of assignment confusion and led to the ball-watching incident on the goal. It was a curious decision that would only be justified if Gatti truly was out of it and in need of a breather.

Sunday's away game to Fiorentina is the last game ahead of the international break. The Viola just escaped the relegation zone last week, but that hardly ever matters in a game at the Stadio Artemio Franchi, where Fiorentina and their fans area always ready to try to ruin their rival's day. It'll be a hot and hostile atmosphere that Juve will need to deal with in order to get three points.

articles.title: Premier League legends at odds over 'overrated' Bradley Barcola following $167 million move
articles.summary: Former Liverpool defender Glen Johnson has hit back at claims from Arsenal legend and FIFA World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit that the Reds paid over the odds f...
articles.body:
Glen Johnson has addressed comments from France FIFA World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit, suggesting Liverpool overpaid for 'overrated' £123 million ($166.6 million) summer acquisition Bradley Barcola. The former Reds defender has expressed confidence that the winger will find his form following a challenging beginning to his Anfield tenure.

Barcola toiled in an unaccustomed striker's position on Wednesday as Liverpool's flawless UEFA Champions League league phase record ended with a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahçe in Istanbul.

The France international had shone in his prior Champions League road fixture, delivering an impressive hat-trick during the 6-3 winat LASK.

However, those strikes represent the sole goals Barcola has managed across his 13 outings for the Reds following his blockbuster transfer from European champions Paris Saint-Germain on August 31.

Earlier this month, former Arsenal, Barcelona, and Chelsea midfielder Petit, who captured the World Cup with France in 1998, stated via the Liverpool Echo : "£120m? I would never put that price tag on the table. We all know that in France.

"We know that he is a quality player, he could sometimes be great, but he doesn't have consistency during games. He was good most of the time with Paris because of the whole team behind him. I would probably have spent £60m or £70m, maximum. That's my opinion. It's becoming common now that English clubs are spending so much money on overrated players."

However, Johnson, who registered 200 appearances for Liverpool with nine goals and 13 assists following his £17.5 million (around $29 million) transfer from Portsmouth in June 2009, considers Barcola "world-class" and argues he shouldn't be evaluated solely on his price tag.

He said: "I don't think Barcola is overrated. I think he's world-class. I've been a fan of his for a long time. I think he's brilliant.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"I think what Manu Petit is trying to say is that he wasn't worth that money. I think that's what he meant. There's no doubt about his talent, his ability and obviously fans have the right to think whether he's world class or not. That's up to them.

"But I think what Manu was actually meaning was the fact that there's some other players who are really good that are going for half the money.

"So I think he meant more of that, than actually being not as good as people say. Because that's two different things. You need the talent there to compete with each other. I was hoping Liverpool would sign him before. The financial stuff, that has nothing to do with us. We just want to see the best players at Liverpool and how they can get it done.

"And the best players will play. And the ones that aren't playing have to improve. It can only be a good level of competition."

With Barcola's French international teammate Hugo Ekitike still on the sidelines, Reds manager Andoni Iraola nevertheless boasts an abundance of attacking talent to call upon.

Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz, alongside Barcola, are all vying for the two wide positions, while Lewis Koumas has impressed the new head coach sufficiently to emerge as a credible backup to Alexander Isak up front as Ekitike continues his rehabilitation from a serious injury.

Isak notched his seventh goal in 13 appearances when he headed Liverpool ahead against Fenerbahçe, and after a difficult debut season with the 20-time English champions hampered by fitness concerns, the £125 million recruit from Newcastle United is beginning to hit his stride

"No one wants to be injured, but I think it's very important for attacking players to have games under your belt," said Johnson, speaking to PariuriX.com . "A rhythm of games to find that flair and the confidence to pull the things off that they can do so well.

"So it's hard for them if they're in one game, out for two, back for two, out for one. It's very hard to get that consistency. But his ability is not questionable. It might be hard to rely on him in terms of when he's available."

Liverpool round out their schedule before the international break on Sunday with a trip to struggling Crystal Palace in the Premier League.

articles.title: Notre Dame releases hype video ahead of big showdown versus Miami
articles.summary: Notre Dame will have a No. 4-No. 1 matchup vs. Miami that's been 38 years in the making. The Irish hyped up the South Bend faithful in a video.
articles.body:
Notre Dame is just a day away from the biggest game of its season .

It's the No. 4 Fighting Irish against top-ranked Miami at Notre Dame Stadium Saturday evening, with the fate of the College Football Playoff push on the line.

The video begins with famous words from the late, great head coach Lou Holtz: "You gotta believe. This school was founded on faith and on belief."

It then shifts to narration by actor and comedian Jason Sudeikis, who is slated to be the guest picker on College GameDay Saturday morning.

"History is a funny thing," Sudeikis said. "Years go by, names change, generations come and go. But history has a way of repeating itself. These teams, these stakes, on the biggest stage...Notre Dame and Miami: College Football's biggest names, meeting with everything on the line. Maybe that's why this all feels so familiar. We've seen it before."

As the video unveils the words of Holtz once again, "If you believe it, you'll feel it," it shows archived footage of No. 4 Notre Dame's 31-30 upset over No. 1 Miami in 1988.

See the best photos from Notre Dame's 35-13 win over Navy

The Irish's monumental victory that year propelled them to the national title and an undefeated season.

"1988...that is history," Sudeikis said. "It leaves a blueprint. It shows what it took. It reminds us what's at stake, but we're not here to repeat history. We're here to make it."

The video then reveals a clip of coach Marcus Freeman hyping up his Notre Dame squad this season.

"Do it for somebody else. Do it for these guys in this room," Freeman said.

It ends with a Sudiekis hinting at what could occur if Notre Dame, a significant favorite against Miami this weekend, pulls off the same win again 38 years later.

"History doesn't decide what happens next. That decision belongs to us," Sudiekis said.

The Irish (7-1) and the Hurricanes (8-0) will face off at 7:30 p.m. Saturday on NBC.
